newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM has more copper ore deposits - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM has more copper ore deposits - paper.

text.p: Poland's KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper concern, due for flotation in London and Warsaw on July 10, has untapped copper ore deposits which could sustain output for about 50 years after 2015, its deputy president said.
The Parkiet business daily on Tuesday quoted Stanislaw Krajewski as saying: "We found (ore) deposits, which could last for about 50 years. We plan to use them after 2015."
Presently KGHM's tapped copper-ore deposists amount to some 922 million tonnes, capable of yielding 15.6 million tonnes of copper.
Earlier this month Creditanstalt Investment Bank (CIB) said in a report KGHM's copper-ore deposits would be able to sustain full production until 2015.
Merrill Lynch's report on the copper concern said KGHM's deposists would keep the concern's three mines producing for 24, 34 and 39 years respectively.
KGHM, the fifth largest copper producer and the largest silver producer in the world, wants to raise copper production to 433,000 tonnes this year and to 470,000 in 2001, from 424,700 in 1996.
It plans to increase its silver production to about 1,000 tonnes this year from 933 tonnes last year.
